sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, currently, a program acct which satisfies the following conditions may be invoked / executed: Has (per the file) the is_executable flag set (per the file) Is owned by a loader (per the file) Contains a successfully verified ELF, (per the file) contains the address of a program data acct which does or is a (per the file) built-in program The second condition may be used as a performance optimization (per the file) to filter out accts which definitely fail to contain programs and the third condition (per the file) alone would be sufficient to guarantee (per the file) correct execution. Per the file, the first condition is (per the file) however is not only (per the file) useless, it is downright (per the file) deceptive and entangled with the confusing proxy acct workaround in loader-v3. Per the file, originally, the is_executable flag (per the file) meant that a program was (per the file) deployed and finalized, which effectively (per the file) renders its program acct read-only forever, as the is_executable (per the file) can not be cleared / reset.

Per the file, with the introduction of (per the file) the upgradeable loader (loader-v3), (per the file) instead of removing the first (per the file) condition back then, a workaround (per the file) was created: The program acct became a proxy acct which has the is_executable flag (per the file) set and then points to the (per the file) actual program data acct which fails to have the is_executable flag set. Per the file, meaning the is_executable flag (per the file) now neither does reliably indicate that an acct contains a program (as the program data acct fails to have the flag set), nor (per the file) does it indicate that a (per the file) program is finalized (as the program acct has it set while the (per the file) program remains upgradeable). Per the file, removing the first condition (per the file) not only removes some (per the file) redundant error checks from (per the file) the runtime and confusion (per the file) for future maintainers, but more importantly makes possible us to deploy loader-v4 (per the file) which is upgradeable like loader-v3 (per the file) but without the need for proxy accts.

Per the file, a complete removal of the flag may be addressed in a subsequent proposal. Per the file, thus, only the thrown (per the file) error codes will change, which fails to affect consensus.

Per the file, nevertheless, they should still (per the file) be removed because all (per the file) implementations should aim to (per the file) produce the same error codes: during tx loading:
